title: The copilot that offered a DELETE
blurb: The draft skipped validation and a generated statement ran writes.
prompt: A user asked the copilot to clean up stale rows and the generated DELETE was returned without a dry-run because the draft only validated short statements. The same endpoint executed caller-supplied SQL on the primary. Review it, fix it, and prove generated statements are read-only and every one is validated.
aiNote: The draft skips warehouse validation for statements over 100 characters and returns the SQL even when the dry-run errors, and the results endpoint executes whatever statement it receives on the primary connection.
testIdea: Ask for a DELETE and assert it is either refused or clearly marked non-executable; throw a validation timeout and assert no SQL is returned; send a two-statement payload to the results endpoint and assert 400.
followUps: How would you tell a read-only statement from a write without a parser?
What cost estimate would you show before running a query and why?
Where should row-level permissions for the copilot live?
